_: The averages the dashboard sets a game's own numbers beside, each with where it comes from. The comparison is a game launched with no marketing wherever a figure for one exists; where none does, the row says whose average it is. Rates are shares (0.267 is 26.7%), times are seconds. Update a number only with its source. Apple's and Google's peer percentiles come from signed-in consoles, so they are kept in the database (the manual.apple_peers and manual.google_peers facts), not here; an entry's peers_where, peers_source and peers_url say whose they are. An entry's ios or android block replaces its fields on that platform's view; a figure published for both platforms together serves both.

downloads_month.label: Total downloads
downloads_month.what: First downloads in a game's first month on one store
downloads_month.where: The median of nine games launched in 2026 with no marketing, as their makers reported them; the middle of the nine ran 30 to 120, and two passed 500. One solo developer's zero-marketing app got 97 (habitdoom.com).

android.where: Three games launched in 2026 with no marketing gave Google Play's own count: 31 installs in the first month (Google Play only), about 70, and 11 in three weeks, as their makers reported them. Across US Google Play, the median app released in the first half of 2026 shows 50 to 99 installs two to nine months on (GetAppNiche, counting only apps still listed).

store_conversion.label: Store conversion
store_conversion.what: Downloads and redownloads for every time the listing was shown: downloads for every impression
store_conversion.where: AppTweak's 2025 US App Store average for Games, downloads for every impression, from apps whose publishers use its tool; Simulation games average 2.7%. Apple's own peer percentiles replace it once they are read into the database.
store_conversion.peers_where: Apple's own figures for free apps with in-app purchases in the same category, marketed or not: the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile.

page_to_download.label: Page to download
page_to_download.what: First downloads made from the product page for every time it was opened
page_to_download.where: AppTweak's 2025 US App Store average for Games, from apps whose publishers use its tool. Simulation games average 33.4% and Adventure games 8.6%; the 8.6% the article leads with is all categories, and it says 25% a few lines on. Four launches with no marketing reported 14% to 30%.

android.label: Store listing to install
android.what: Installs made from the Google Play store listing for every visitor to it
android.where: AppTweak's 2025 US Google Play average across all categories, from apps whose publishers use its tool: first installs over store listing visits. Mistplay, citing Business of Apps, puts Google Play games at 17.9%, Simulation at 16.7% and Casual at 14.3%. Google's own peer percentiles replace this once they are on record.
android.peers_where: Google's own figures for the apps in the game's Play Console peer group, marketed or not: store listing visitors who installed, each day, the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile, averaged over the days read.
android.peers_source: Google Play Console, Compare to peers

search_clicks.label: Search clicks
search_clicks.what: Product page views for every time the listing was shown in App Store search
search_clicks.where: AppFollow, US App Store search, August 2026: the lowest and highest category median. It names no category for either end, and Games has the lowest search install rate (2.6%), so expect the low end. On the App Store a shopper can tap Get in the results without opening the page.

ios.where: Median and bottom quarter: GameAnalytics' 2025 figures for 16,000 mobile games on iOS and Android together; it publishes no median for one platform alone. Top quarter: iOS games alone, 31% to 33% on day 1 in 2024 (Android 25% to 27%). No figure exists for small or unmarketed games alone.

android.where: Median and bottom quarter: GameAnalytics' 2025 figures for 16,000 mobile games on iOS and Android together; it publishes no median for one platform alone. Top quarter: Android games alone, 25% to 27% on day 1 in 2024 (iOS 31% to 33%). No figure exists for small or unmarketed games alone.

retention.what: New players who play again that many days later
retention.where: GameAnalytics' median for 16,000 mobile games on iOS and Android together, with 1,000 or more monthly players in 2025, with the bottom and top quarter of games as the range. No figure exists for small or unmarketed games alone.

session_length.label: Session length
session_length.what: The average length of one play session
session_length.where: GameAnalytics' median for mobile games in 2025, about 3.3 minutes; the top quarter of games reach about 5.2.

playtime.label: Play time a day
playtime.what: How long a player plays on a day they play
playtime.where: GameAnalytics' median for mobile games in 2025, about 12 minutes; the top quarter of games reach 22 to 24.

android.what: Time in the game per daily active player
android.peers_where: Google's own figures for the apps in the game's Play Console peer group, marketed or not: time in the app per daily active user, each day, the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile, averaged over the days read.
android.peers_source: Google Play Console, Compare to peers

dau_mau.label: Daily ÷ monthly players
dau_mau.what: The share of the month's players who play on a given day

android.peers_where: Google's own figures for the apps in the game's Play Console peer group, marketed or not: daily active users over monthly active users, each day, the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile, averaged over the days read.
android.peers_source: Google Play Console, Compare to peers

user_loss.label: Players lost
user_loss.what: Players who uninstalled from all their devices, over those who still have it on an active one; less is better

android.peers_where: Google's own figures for the apps in the game's Play Console peer group, marketed or not: users lost a day over the installed audience, the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile, averaged over the days read.
android.peers_source: Google Play Console, Compare to peers

paying_players.label: Players who pay
paying_players.what: New players who buy within their first 7 days
paying_players.where: Two small iOS games with no marketing had 0.7% and 1.1% of downloads pay (their developer's own numbers, 2014); in commercial free games 1.9% of monthly players buy (Swrve, 2016). At 100 downloads that is zero to two people.

android.where: RevenueCat's median for 115,000 subscription apps: 0.9% of Android downloads paid within 35 days, against 2.6% on iOS. No figure exists for Android games alone, or for games with no marketing.

buyer_ratio.label: Monthly buyers
buyer_ratio.what: The share of the month's players who bought something in it

android.peers_where: Google's own figures for the apps in the game's Play Console peer group, marketed or not: buyers in the last 28 days over monthly active users, each day, the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile, averaged over the days read.
android.peers_source: Google Play Console, Compare to peers

proceeds_per_payer.label: Proceeds per paying player
proceeds_per_payer.what: What a paying player brings in after the store's cut
proceeds_per_payer.peers_where: Apple's own figures for free apps with in-app purchases in the same category, marketed or not, a week at a time: the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile.

purchase_value.label: Revenue per purchase
purchase_value.what: What one purchase brings in, on average over a month

android.peers_where: Google's own figures for the apps in the game's Play Console peer group, marketed or not: revenue over purchases in the last 28 days, in US dollars, each day, the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile, averaged over the days read.
android.peers_source: Google Play Console, Compare to peers

revenue_month.label: Revenue, first month
revenue_month.what: What players spent in a game's first month
revenue_month.where: Six games launched in 2026 with no marketing made $0, $0, about $0.10, $0.10, $3 and $6 in their first month or two, ads included.
